10 Thoughts From the Sidelines: Florida 52, Ole Miss 28
candidates.chrisContext: Column | By Chris Spears, GatorBait Media Florida 52, Ole Miss 28. The scoreboard told you who won. The sideline told you what kind of team this is. 1. Florida has an identity again. The Gators want to run the football, and they want you to know it’s coming. Line up, lean on people and find out who still wants to tackle Jadan Baugh in the fourth quarter. Against the No. 4 team in the country, Florida ran for 302 yards. 2. Jadan Baugh is the compass. Twenty-nine carries, 142 yards, three touchdowns. That made five straight 100-yard games, a run only Emmitt Smith and Fred Taylor had put together at Florida. When the Gators need four yards, everybody in the stadium knows who’s getting the ball. He usually gets six. 3. Duke Clark means no intermission. You survive Baugh, he trots to the sideline, and in walks Duke Clark: 12 carries, 126 yards. That’s not a backup. That’s a second problem. His 45-yard touchdown came minutes after Ole Miss cut it to 17-14 and started to believe. “I thought Duke played out of his mind, and he’s got all the ability in the world.” — Jon Sumrall 4.
